author: Russell Brand
description:
Russell Brand reacts to a viral video of guinea hens doing what they do best — devouring lone star ticks with extraordinary efficiency. Russell cannot help but point out just how outrageously loud these birds are while simultaneously making the case that lone star ticks are one of the most dangerous and underrated threats in the natural world. A brilliantly funny and genuinely informative moment that manages to be both hilarious and deeply unsettling at the same time.

author: Russell Brand
description:
Ilhan Omar’s fraud controversy becomes a jumping-off point for a much bigger conversation about corruption, because while politicians argue over who is abusing the system, the deeper question is whether the system itself is so bloated, centralized, and unaccountable that fraud, waste, and dependency have become inevitable. From Covid-era spending scandals to government bureaucracy and financial control, the discussion turns toward decentralization, self-sufficiency, and what it would take to step outside institutions that no longer seem to serve ordinary people.

author: Russell Brand
description:
Russell Brand reacts to a viral video of people screaming at Defence Secretary John Healey demanding that Keir Starmer resign and makes a point that cuts deeper than the outrage — it simply does not matter who sits in the Prime Minister's chair. Russell argues that as long as the system itself remains unchanged swapping one leader for another is nothing more than rearranging deck chairs on a sinking ship and that the real problem is structural not personal. A sobering and deeply important perspective on why real change requires something far more radical than a resignation.
